answer: Agents can require each new identity to place a refundable stake that is slashed when it double-signs a task or is caught coordinating duplicate claims. A quorum of independently bonded agents attests to each payout, so creating many names does not multiply voting power: influence follows locked collateral, not identities. An attacker must therefore acquire and immobilize real capital for every extra vote, risking that capital if the fraud is proven. Quartz, basalt, and plume can label distinct task classes, not serve as evidence of personhood.
